Feature.title: Feature Flags
Feature.enableIPv6Desc: Lets b4 process IPv6 packets, DNS answers and firewall rules. With this off b4 ignores IPv6 entirely: it does not disable IPv6 on the router, and sites a set targets stay reachable over IPv6 with none of the set's strategies applied.
Feature.ipv6BypassWarning: This host has a working global IPv6 address while b4 is processing IPv4 only. Anything that reaches a target over IPv6 goes out with no set applied. Turn IPv6 support on, or leave the DNS IPv4 fallback enabled so matched domains resolve to IPv4.
Feature.firewallMonitorHelp: Interval for monitoring B4 iptables/nftables rules

Feature.firewallMonitorWarning: Warning: This disables automatic monitoring of B4 iptables/nftables
Feature.engineModeHelp: How b4 receives packets. NFQUEUE uses iptables/nftables rules; TUN routes target traffic through a virtual interface, useful where NFQUEUE kernel modules are unavailable.
Feature.tunOutInterfaceDesc: Where b4 sends processed packets. Auto follows the system default route and re-points automatically when the WAN/VPN changes; pick an interface to pin it.
Feature.tunOutInterfaceAutoHint: Auto mode tracks the system default route and re-points the uplink automatically when the WAN or VPN changes.
Feature.tunOutGatewayHelp: Gateway IP for the uplink. Leave empty to auto-detect from the current default route.
Feature.tunOutGatewayAuto: Resolved automatically from the default route while the uplink is on Auto.
Feature.tunAddressHelp: Address/prefix for the TUN device. Must not overlap your LAN or VPN subnets.
Feature.tunDeviceNameHelp: Name of the virtual interface b4 creates.

Feature.masqueradeAllInterfaces: Masquerade will apply to all output interfaces if none is selected.
Feature.networkInterfacesDesc: Only inspect packets whose interface is one of these. For forwarded traffic that is the interface the packet leaves by, which a tunnel or a VPN client can change without touching this list. Empty = every interface, which is what almost every setup wants.
Feature.listenAllInterfaces: B4 will listen on all available interfaces if none are selected.
Feature.interfaceFilterSeesNothing: Nothing B4 has seen has left by {{selected}}. Traffic is going out {{seen}}, none of it is being inspected, and no set is being applied to it. Clear the selection to watch every interface.

Socks5.title: SOCKS5 Proxy
Socks5.description: Built-in SOCKS5 proxy that routes traffic through DPI bypass engine
Socks5.enableDesc: Built-in SOCKS5 proxy that routes traffic through DPI bypass engine
Socks5.bindAddressHelp: IP to bind (0.0.0.0 = all, 127.0.0.1 = localhost only)
Socks5.sourcesDesc: Restricts which client addresses may open a SOCKS5 connection. An empty list accepts every source. Chrome and Chromium do not support SOCKS5 username and password authentication, so for those clients a source list is the only way to limit access.
Socks5.addSourceHelp: A single IP or a CIDR range, IPv4 or IPv6. Loopback is not implied: add 127.0.0.1/32 for a client running on the router itself. Applies on save, no restart needed.
Socks5.sourcesEmpty: No source restriction: every client that reaches the port may connect.
Socks5.noDevices: No devices with an IPv4 address
Socks5.sourceInvalid: Enter an IP address or a CIDR range, for example 192.168.1.50 or 192.168.1.0/24
Socks5.sourceAll: A /0 range covers every address and switches the restriction off. Leave the list empty instead.
Socks5.sourcesNote: A source list is a network gate, the same kind of control as a firewall rule, not an authentication factor: addresses can be spoofed, a DHCP lease can move to another device, and a host that is itself a router stands for everything behind it. b4 adds no firewall rule for the SOCKS5 port, so bind the proxy to the LAN address to keep it off the WAN.
Socks5.openRelayWarning: The proxy has no credentials and no source list. Any client that can reach the listening address and port can relay traffic through it.

MTProto.title: MTProto Proxy
MTProto.serverDesc: A Telegram proxy that clients connect to with a secret, on this LAN or remotely, for example from a cellular network. Not needed for the 'Telegram over WebSocket' routing mode.
MTProto.bindAddressHelp: IP to bind (0.0.0.0 = all, 127.0.0.1 = localhost only)
MTProto.maxConnectionsHelp: Maximum concurrent client connections (default: 2048). Each Telegram client uses several connections for chats and media; raise this for a shared proxy with many users.
MTProto.tcpUserTimeoutHelp: Force-close a connection after this many seconds of unacknowledged data, so a phone that dropped off mobile network is detected in ~2 min instead of ~15 min (default: 120, -1 to disable).
MTProto.idleTimeoutHelp: Close a relayed session after this many seconds with no traffic in either direction, freeing sessions held by a backgrounded client (default: 300, -1 to disable).
MTProto.fakeSNIHelp: Domain to impersonate in the TLS handshake.
MTProto.cfWorkerDomainHelp: Free per-user WebSocket relay (workers.dev). Recommended when media, reactions, or stickers fail to load. Reaches all data centers and avoids the shared-domain rate limits. Comma-separate multiple workers. Click the icon for setup.
MTProto.dcRelayHelp: External relay address (host:port) to reach Telegram DCs when blocked by IP
MTProto.dcRelayHelpButton: Show socat commands for relay setup
MTProto.dcRelayHelpIntro: Run these commands on your VPS to forward each Telegram DC to the relay port B4 uses. They point at the public data-center addresses B4 dials over direct TCP. The media DC 203 reuses the DC 2 port, so it needs no command of its own.
MTProto.dcRelayHelpEmpty: Set the DC Relay address first (e.g. {{example}}). The base port determines the rest of the mapping.
MTProto.dcRelayHelpFailed: Could not load the data-center addresses. Try the Refresh button.
MTProto.dcRelayHelpRefreshFailed: Could not refresh Telegram's DC list. The commands below use B4's built-in data-center addresses and are still correct.
MTProto.dcRelayHelpHint: Open these ports on the VPS firewall: {{ports}}.
MTProto.dcRelayHelpV6Note: The IPv6 data-center addresses are built into B4 and are not affected by Refresh, because Telegram's proxy config lists IPv4 only. Media DC 203 has no IPv6 address and shares the DC 2 relay port, so media is carried by the DC 2 command; if media stops loading, switch that one command back to IPv4.
MTProto.relaySetup: DC Relay requires a VPS setup. Read the setup guide
MTProto.secretsDesc: Create a separate secret per user so you can name, disable, or revoke access individually. The logs show which secret each connection used.
MTProto.webProxyDesc: Serve the MTProxy stream over ordinary HTTPS. Telegram Desktop 7.1.1 and later loads the relay hostname in a hidden WebView and tunnels MTProto through it, so the client opens no MTProto socket of its own and the traffic looks like a browser visiting a website.
MTProto.webProxyHostnameHelp: A bare public hostname, no scheme, port or path. Punycode (xn--) form for international names.
MTProto.webProxyRequirements: The hostname must resolve to this instance and serve valid TLS on port 443, with the site root reaching b4. A hostname of its own is required: b4 answers every path on it, so the b4 interface is not reachable there. The connection link is in the share dialog of a secret.
MTProto.secretMaxNetworksHelp: Refuse this secret once it is in use from more than this many client networks at once. Devices sharing one internet connection count as one network, so a person moving between home, mobile data and work needs a few. 0 means no limit.
MTProto.shareHostHelp: Address the recipient device will use to reach this proxy. LAN IP for local devices, public IP or DDNS hostname for remote use (port forwarding required).
MTProto.upstreamDesc: How b4 reaches Telegram data centers, both for the proxy server and for the 'Telegram over WebSocket' routing mode in sets, so it applies even when the proxy server is off. The routing mode always uses Auto; the transport mode below applies to the proxy server only.
MTProto.bridgeWaitHelp: How long the 'Telegram over WebSocket' bridge waits for a client's first handshake byte before dropping the connection. Telegram opens connections to a data center before it has anything to send, and a client that gets closed too early counts it as a failure and keeps rotating data centers (default: 180, -1 to wait indefinitely).
MTProto.upstreamTcpDesc: Fastest. Use when this host can reach 149.154.0.0/16 directly.
MTProto.upstreamAutoDesc: Try WebSocket first via kws*.web.telegram.org, fall back to direct TCP. Recommended for censored networks.
MTProto.upstreamWsDesc: Strict WebSocket transport via kws*.web.telegram.org. No TCP fallback.
MTProto.wsCustomDomainHelp: Optional extra domain (e.g. your-domain.com) that proxies WebSocket traffic to Telegram. b4 prepends kws1., kws2., ... per DC automatically. Independent of the CF proxy fallback below.
MTProto.wsEndpointHostHelp: Override the IP used when WS uses native kws*.web.telegram.org SNI. Default: 149.154.167.220. Leave empty for default. Does not affect the custom WebSocket domain path.
MTProto.cfProxyEnabledHelp: Use a rotating pool of Cloudflare-proxied domains as a fallback when Telegram's native edge can't reach a data center (notably DC 1, which is needed for media in foreign channels). The pool is refreshed once an hour from the URL below.
MTProto.cfProxyURLHelp: Source for the encoded CF-proxy domain list. Default is tg-ws-proxy's GitHub. Replace with your own if you host your own list.
MTProto.dcFallbackEnabledHelp: Telegram's data-center IP list is fetched from Telegram's official endpoint first. When that endpoint is blocked, b4 falls back to the mirror below. The mirror receives your IP address but no other data. Disable to use only Telegram's official endpoint.
MTProto.dcFallbackURLHelp: Source for the fallback data-center list, used only when Telegram's official endpoint is unreachable. Default is the b4 author's mirror. Set your own mirror here if you host one.
MTProto.testDirectTcpHelp: Probes DC 2 over direct TCP to Telegram, bypassing the DC Relay. Use to isolate whether issues come from the relay or from Telegram itself.
MTProto.upstreamAutoRelayDesc: DC Relay is configured: relay TCP is tried first, WebSocket as fallback.
MTProto.shareWebFooter: Carries the padded secret form Telegram Desktop accepts for WEB entries.

MSSClamping.title: Global MSS Clamping
MSSClamping.description: Clamp TCP Maximum Segment Size to force data fragmentation
MSSClamping.enableDesc: Clamp MSS on all SYN packets via firewall rules (nftables/iptables)
MSSClamping.mssSizeHelp: Lower values = more fragmentation. 88 is commonly used for YouTube bypass.
MSSClamping.info: Reduces the TCP Maximum Segment Size on SYN/SYN-ACK packets for all TCP port 443 traffic, forcing data fragmentation. Most DPI systems cannot reassemble fragmented ClientHello. For per-device MSS clamping, use the Device Filtering settings.

IPHealth.title: IP Health
IPHealth.description: How long a destination stays marked unreachable
IPHealth.info: IP block detection is configured per set, but whether an address answers is a property of the address and the path to it, not of the set that matched it. The verdict is therefore shared across sets, and so is how long it lasts.
IPHealth.retestIntervalHelper: How long a destination stays marked unreachable before the router tests it again. Blocks get lifted and addresses get reassigned, so a verdict that never expires would strand devices on a stale one. This is also how long recovery takes, since a condemned address is reset before it can complete a handshake.

Dns.title: DNS
Dns.description: How b4 resolves DNS for matched sets, and how it handles DNS over TCP
Dns.info: A set with its own DNS server answers matched domains through that server. Queries over UDP are handled by the packet queue; queries over TCP are redirected into b4 on the port below. Domains that match no set, and sets with no DNS server, are always passed to the resolver the client chose.
Dns.tcpEnableDesc: Without this, a client that falls back to TCP reaches the upstream resolver and the set's DNS server is skipped
Dns.tcpPortHelp: Local port b4 redirects TCP port 53 to. Change it only if something else already uses this port.
Dns.queryTimeoutHelp: How long to wait for the set's DNS server before answering SERVFAIL. Applies to UDP and TCP alike.
Dns.tcpIdleHelp: How long an idle DNS-over-TCP connection is held open for further queries
Dns.tcpIoHelp: Deadline for a single query or answer on an established connection
Dns.tcpDialHelp: How long to wait when forwarding an unmatched TCP query to the resolver the client chose
Dns.ipv4FallbackDesc: While b4 processes IPv4 only, strip AAAA records from answers for domains a set matched, so the client connects over IPv4 where the set's strategies apply. Turn this off to keep the AAAA records and let those domains go out over IPv6 unprocessed.
Dns.ipv4FallbackIdle: Not used while IPv6 support is on - b4 processes IPv6 itself, so AAAA answers are kept.

Mcp.title: MCP server
Mcp.description: Lets an AI app (Claude Desktop, Cursor, LM Studio) read b4's state over the Model Context Protocol at /api/mcp.
Mcp.allowWritesHelp: Lets the AI change any setting inside a strategy set, plus the MTProto and SOCKS5 subsystems. Credentials, the web server, the capture engine and the firewall backend stay read-only. Any change can be undone by asking the AI to revert it.
Mcp.allowWritesWarning: The AI can change settings, not just read them. The AI app should ask for approval before each change; do not approve one that is not understood. A change that turns out to be wrong can be undone by asking the AI to revert it.
Mcp.allowProbesHelp: Lets the AI make b4 fetch a domain to see whether it actually loads, and run a discovery search that tries strategies until one works. Off by default: these send real traffic from the router. Separate from configuration changes, because emitting traffic is a different permission from editing settings.
Mcp.allowProbesWarning: The AI can make the router fetch sites and run discovery. A discovery run takes minutes, sends heavy traffic, holds firewall rules for its duration and blocks the watchdog while it runs. Private and local addresses are refused.
Mcp.noAuthWarning: Web authentication is off, so anyone who can reach this port can read b4's status, configuration and diagnostics through MCP. Fine on a trusted home network; set a username and password under Web Server if the port is reachable from elsewhere.
Mcp.noTokenWarning: No MCP token is set, so clients have to use a web login token instead. Those expire after a day and are discarded when b4 restarts, which leaves the AI app unable to connect until you paste a new one. Generate an MCP token to avoid that.
Mcp.tokenHelp: Survives restarts, unlike a web login token. Grants access to /api/mcp and nothing else.

targets.tlsHelperText: Prefer a specific TLS version (used as a fallback when no exact-version match exists)
targets.ipVersionHelperText: Prefer IPv4 or IPv6 traffic (used as a fallback when no exact-version match exists)
targets.domainOnlyDesc: Match these domains only by the name in the handshake, never by their IP address. Use it on shared CDN addresses, where a neighbouring domain on the same IP would otherwise be pulled into this set and given its strategy. Routing selects traffic by IP address, so a set with this on routes only the addresses you list explicitly.
targets.catchAllDomainsDesc: Adds the {{value}} entry, which matches every domain.
targets.catchAllDomainsActive: This set matches every domain. A domain listed literally in any other set is handled there first, whatever position either set holds in the list, so this set picks up only what nothing else claims. That applies to DPI matching; for routing it steers only the addresses this set has actually resolved, so it is not a substitute for matching every IP address.
targets.catchAllDomainNotice: Matches every domain. "{{value}}" will be added.
targets.wildcardStrippedNotice: b4 already matches subdomains, so "{{from}}" will be added as "{{to}}".
targets.catchAllIpsActive: This set matches every IP address. For DPI matching, a narrower range in any other set is handled there first, whatever position either set holds in the list, so this set picks up only what nothing else claims. Routing is decided by firewall rules instead, where an overlapping set can win regardless of that order, so avoid pairing this with another routing set covering the same addresses.
targets.catchAllIpNotice: Matches every IP address. "{{value}}" will be added.
targets.escalateHelper: If this set keeps failing for a site, b4 will use the chosen set for that site instead. After a while, b4 tries this set again.

tcp.sectionDescription: Configure TCP packet handling and DPI bypass techniques

general.seg2delayHelper: Delay between TCP segments. Use a range for random delay per packet.
general.portFilterHelper: Match specific TCP ports (Telegram, XMPP, etc.) - port 443 is always included
general.dropSackDesc: Strip Selective Acknowledgment from TCP headers to confuse stateful DPI
general.dupAlert: Some ISPs throttle by randomly dropping outgoing packets to specific IP ranges (e.g. Telegram subnets). Duplication sends multiple copies of each packet. When enabled, all other DPI evasion is bypassed for this set. Applies to all configured TCP ports.
general.dupEnableDesc: Drop original packet and send multiple copies via raw socket
general.dupCountHelper: Number of packet copies to send (original is dropped)
general.ibdAlert: Some server addresses are dropped by the firewall at the IP level rather than by domain name, and no bypass strategy applies because nothing ever reaches the server. Two shapes are detected: a handshake that completes and then swallows the TLS ClientHello, and a SYN that is never answered at all, which is what an address-level block looks like. A CDN often answers DNS with several addresses of which only some are blocked, so the site works or hangs depending on which one the device picked.
general.ibdEnableDesc: Detect destinations that never answer and act on them
general.ibdHealDnsDesc: Also strip unreachable addresses out of DNS answers. If every address is unreachable, the last one that worked for that domain is answered instead
general.ibdSynDetectDesc: Catch address-level blocks, where the handshake never completes
general.ibdSynThresholdHelper: How many unanswered SYNs before the router tests the address itself. Nothing is acted on until that test also fails, which keeps a slow or briefly unreachable server from being condemned.
general.ibdThresholdHelper: How many unanswered ClientHello retransmissions before declaring the destination blocked. Applies after the handshake completed, so it covers a stateful block rather than an address-level one.
general.ibdThresholdWarn: A low threshold may cause false positives - a single dropped packet or slow server could be mistaken for an IP block.
general.ibdTimeoutHelper: Alternative trigger: time since first attempt with no response
general.ibdHealTtlHelper: TTL written into curated DNS answers. Keep it short so a device picks up a recovered address quickly instead of caching the curated answer for hours.
general.ibdCacheDesc: Remember blocked IPs so future connections get instant reset without waiting
general.rstAlert: DPI systems can inject fake TCP RST packets to kill your connections. This feature records the TTL (hop count) from the real server's first response and drops any RST packet whose TTL doesn't match — a strong indicator that it was injected from a different network position.
general.rstEnableDesc: Drop RST packets with mismatched TTL to prevent DPI-injected connection resets
general.rstTtlToleranceHelper: Maximum allowed difference between the server's reference TTL and an incoming RST packet's TTL
general.mssEnableDesc: Override TCP MSS for connections matching this set's IP, GeoIP, or device targets
general.mssScopeHint: MSS is set on the TCP SYN, before the TLS handshake. It can only be scoped by IP / GeoIP / source device. SNI domain, GeoSite and TLS version filters do not participate in MSS clamping.
general.mssScopeRequired: Add an IP, GeoIP, or source device target before enabling per-set MSS.
general.mssSizeHelper: Typical TSPU workaround for Smart TVs on YouTube: 88

splitting.strategyPoolDesc: Select multiple strategies to randomize per connection. When active, a random strategy is picked from the pool for each new packet. Leave empty to use the selected method above.
splitting.strategyPoolActive: {{count}} strategies in pool — each connection will use a random one
splitting.oobAlert: Inserts a byte with TCP URG flag. Server ignores it, but stateful DPI gets confused.
splitting.tlsRecAlert: Splits ClientHello into multiple TLS records. DPI expecting single-record handshake fails to match.
splitting.tlsRecPositionHelper: First TLS record size in bytes
splitting.disabledWarning: Fragmentation disabled. Only fake packets (if enabled) will be used for bypass.

combo.alert: Combo combines multiple split points and sends segments out of order with timing jitter to confuse stateful DPI.
combo.decoyDesc: Send fake ClientHello with whitelisted SNI before real traffic
combo.sniSplitDesc: Split in middle of SNI hostname
combo.noSplits: No splits enabled - packet sent as single segment
combo.shuffleHelper: How to reorder segments before sending
combo.shuffleMiddleDesc: First and last segments stay in place, only the segments between them are shuffled
combo.shuffleFullDesc: All segments, including first and last, are randomly reordered before sending
combo.shuffleReverseDesc: Segments are sent in completely reversed order — last segment first, first segment last
combo.jitterMaxHelper: Max random delay between other segments (μs)
combo.fakePerSegAlert: sends fake overlap packets before each real segment, not just the first. Floods DPI reassembly with garbage.
combo.fakePerSegDesc: Send fake overlap before every segment
combo.fakesPerSegHelper: Number of fake packets before each segment
combo.noSplitPointsWarning: No split points enabled. Enable at least one for Combo to work effectively.

disorder.alert: Disorder sends real TCP segments out of order with timing jitter. No fake packets — exploits DPI that expects sequential data.
disorder.sniSplitDesc: Split around SNI hostname for targeted disruption
disorder.segRandomOrder: Segments sent in random order (example shown)
disorder.timingAlert: Random delay between segments. Used when TCP Seg2Delay is 0.
disorder.jitterWarning: Max jitter should be greater than min jitter for random variation.
disorder.fakePerSegAlert: Multidisorder: sends fake overlap packets before each real segment, not just the first. Floods DPI reassembly with garbage.
disorder.fakePerSegDesc: Send fake overlap before every segment
disorder.fakesPerSegHelper: Number of fake packets before each segment
disorder.seqOverlapAlert: Prepends fake bytes with decreased TCP sequence number. DPI sees fake protocol header, server discards overlap.
disorder.seqOverlapLengthHelper: How many pattern bytes to prepend to a real segment, with its sequence number shifted back by the same amount (0 = off).
disorder.seqovlNote: DPI sees fake header at decreased seq#, server reassembles correctly
disorder.addByteEmpty: Add hex bytes for custom pattern

extSplit.alert: Automatically splits TLS ClientHello just before the SNI extension. DPI sees incomplete extension list and fails to parse SNI.
extSplit.splitNote: Split happens at the yellow line — before SNI extension starts
extSplit.noConfigNeeded: No configuration needed. Uses Reverse Order toggle above and Seg2 Delay from TCP tab.

firstByte.alert: Sends just 1 byte, waits, then sends the rest. Exploits DPI timeout — incomplete TLS record can't be parsed.
firstByte.vizNote: DPI sees 1 byte (TLS record type), waits for more, times out before SNI arrives
firstByte.noConfigNeeded: No configuration needed. Delay controlled by Seg2 Delay in TCP tab (minimum 100ms applied automatically).

tcpIp.smartSniSplitDesc: Automatically split in the middle of the SNI hostname (recommended)
tcpIp.splitMode3seg: 3 segments: split at fixed position AND middle of SNI
tcpIp.splitModeSni: 2 segments: split at middle of SNI hostname
tcpIp.splitModeFixed: 2 segments: split at byte {{pos}} of TLS payload
tcpIp.manualOverride: Manual override — use if Smart SNI Split doesn't work for your ISP
tcpIp.fixedSplitPosHelper: Bytes from TLS payload start (0 = disabled)
tcpIp.bothEnabled: Both enabled → packet splits into 3 segments

fakeSni.title: Fake SNI Packets
fakeSni.enableDesc: Send fake SNI packets before real ClientHello
fakeSni.strategyHelper: How to make fake packets unprocessable by server
fakeSni.payloadDomainHelper: TLS ClientHello will be generated with this domain as SNI
fakeSni.customPayloadHelper: Hex-encoded payload for fake packets (use Capture feature to get real payloads)
fakeSni.noPayloads: No TLS payloads available. Generate optimized payloads (SNI-first for DPI bypass) or upload your own.
fakeSni.noPayloadsHelper: No payloads available. Generate one in Settings first.
fakeSni.navigateSettings: Navigate to Settings to generate or upload TLS ClientHello payloads.
fakeSni.ttlHelper: TTL for fake packets (should expire before server)
fakeSni.applyTtlDesc: Send the fake at the TTL above whatever the fake strategy is. Without this the TTL only applies when the strategy is TTL
fakeSni.matchLengthDesc: Size the fake to the real ClientHello instead of using the payload's own length
fakeSni.md5OnFakeDesc: Put the TCP MD5 option on the fake ClientHello so the server discards it while DPI still reads it
fakeSni.seqOffsetHelper: TCP sequence number offset for pastseq strategy
fakeSni.timestampDecreaseHelper: Amount to decrease TCP timestamp option (default: 600000)
fakeSni.packetCountHelper: Number of fake packets to send
fakeSni.tlsModDesc: Modify fake TLS ClientHello to improve bypass
fakeSni.randomizeTlsRandomDesc: Replace 32-byte Random field in fake packets
fakeSni.dupSessionIdDesc: Copy Session ID from real ClientHello into fake

synFake.title: SYN Fake Packets
synFake.alert: Send fake SYN packets during the TCP handshake phase to pre-confuse DPI state tracking before the real connection starts.
synFake.enableDesc: Send fake SYN packets during handshake (aggressive technique)
synFake.md5Desc: Send fake SYN with TCP MD5 option before real handshake
synFake.payloadLenHelper: 0 = header only, >0 = add fake TLS payload
synFake.ttlHelper: TTL value for SYN fake packets (default 3 if unset)

desync.title: TCP Desync Attack
desync.alert: Desync attacks inject fake TCP control packets (RST/FIN/ACK) with corrupted checksums and low TTL. These packets confuse stateful DPI systems but are discarded by the real server.
desync.descRst: Inject fake RST packets with bad checksums to disrupt DPI state tracking
desync.descFin: Inject fake FIN packets with past sequence numbers to confuse connection state
desync.descAck: Inject fake ACK packets with random future sequence/ack numbers
desync.descCombo: Send RST + FIN + ACK sequence for stronger desync effect
desync.descFull: Full attack: fake SYN, overlapping RSTs, PSH, and URG packets
desync.ttlHelperEnabled: Low TTL ensures packets expire before reaching server
desync.countHelperEnabled: Number of fake packets per desync attack
desync.postDesyncDesc: Send fake RST after ClientHello to evict connection from DPI tracking table

window.title: Window Manipulation
window.alert: Window manipulation sends fake ACK packets with modified TCP window sizes before your real packet. These fakes use low TTL so they expire before reaching the server but confuse middlebox DPI.
window.descOff: No window manipulation - use actual TCP window
window.descZero: Send fake packets: first with window=0, then window=65535
window.descRandom: Send 3-5 fake packets with random window sizes from your list
window.descOscillate: Cycle through your custom window values sequentially
window.oscillateHint: Packets will cycle through these values in order
window.randomHint: Random values will be picked from this list
window.emptyValues: No values configured - defaults will be used

incoming.title: Incoming Response Bypass
incoming.alert: Manipulates incoming server responses to bypass DPI that throttles connections after receiving ~15-20KB. Injects fake packets toward server that DPI sees but die before reaching destination.
incoming.descFake: Inject corrupted ACK packets toward server with low TTL on every incoming data packet
incoming.descReset: Inject fake RST packets when incoming bytes threshold reached
incoming.descFin: Inject fake FIN packets when incoming bytes threshold reached
incoming.descDesync: Inject RST+FIN+ACK combo when incoming bytes threshold reached
incoming.stratDescBadsum: Corrupt TCP checksum only - packets dropped by kernel
incoming.stratDescBadseq: Corrupt sequence number - packets ignored by TCP stack
incoming.stratDescBadack: Corrupt ACK number - packets ignored by TCP stack
incoming.stratDescRand: Randomly pick corruption method per packet
incoming.stratDescAll: Apply all corruptions: bad seq + bad ack + bad checksum
incoming.ttlHelper: Low TTL ensures fakes expire before reaching server
incoming.fakeCountHelper: Number of fake packets per injection
incoming.thresholdMinFake: Not used in fake mode (triggers on every packet)
incoming.thresholdMaxHelper: Threshold randomized between min-max per connection

mutation.title: ClientHello Mutation
mutation.descRandom: Randomize extension order and add noise
mutation.descGrease: Insert GREASE extensions to confuse DPI
mutation.descPadding: Add padding extension to reach target size
mutation.greaseCountHelper: Number of GREASE extensions to insert
mutation.fakeExtCountHelper: Number of fake TLS extensions to insert
mutation.fakeSniHelper: Additional SNI values to inject into ClientHello

udp.sectionDescription: Configure UDP packet processing and QUIC filtering
udp.blockQuicDesc: Match every QUIC packet to this set's targets and answer it with ICMP port unreachable.
udp.blockQuicInfo: Why block QUIC: QUIC payloads are encrypted end to end, so b4 cannot desync the handshake the way it desyncs TLS over TCP. Only decoys and a fragmented Initial are available, and both are weak. Many DPI systems simply blackhole UDP/443, which leaves a video stalling with no error at all. Blocking QUIC here makes the browser fall back to TCP straight away, where b4's strategies do work.
udp.quicSniDesc: Match QUIC whose ClientHello carries an SNI this set targets. This is also how b4 learns which addresses those domains use.
udp.quicAllDesc: Match by SNI, and additionally treat any QUIC packet sent to a destination this set already matches by IP or port as a match, even with no SNI to read.
udp.portFilterHelper: Match specific UDP ports (VoIP, gaming, etc.) - leave empty to disable
udp.filterStunDesc: Ignore STUN packets (recommended for voice/video calls)
udp.sniWarning: SNI matching needs domains: this set targets no domains and no geosite categories, so no QUIC ClientHello can match it. Add domains in the Targets section, or switch matching to By SNI or matched destination so QUIC sent to this set's IP and port targets counts as a match.
udp.modeFakeDesc: Send decoy packets and fragment the Initial (weak against QUIC)
udp.modeDropDesc: Drop matched UDP silently, so the client falls back to TCP once it stops waiting
udp.modeRejectDesc: Answer with ICMP port unreachable so the client falls back to TCP at once (recommended)
udp.offModeInfo: Off: Matched UDP and QUIC leave b4 unchanged. b4 still reads the QUIC ClientHello, so a set targeting domains keeps learning which addresses those domains resolve to.
udp.fakeModeInfo: Fake mode: Matched UDP packets will be preceded by fake packets and fragmented. QUIC payloads are AEAD-protected, so this cannot desync the handshake the way the TCP strategies do. Configure fake packet settings below.
udp.rejectModeInfo: Reject mode: Matched UDP packets will be dropped and an ICMP Port Unreachable response will be sent back to the client, causing immediate TCP fallback without waiting for timeouts. This is the effective answer to a censor that blackholes UDP/443.
udp.dropModeInfo: Drop mode: Matched UDP packets will be dropped, forcing the application to fall back to TCP (e.g., QUIC → HTTPS). The client waits for its own timeout first, so Reject is usually faster.
udp.noProcessingWarning: UDP action is off: Matched UDP and QUIC pass through unchanged. b4 still reads the QUIC ClientHello to learn which addresses this set's domains use, but it does not alter, drop or reject anything.
udp.strategyTtlDesc: Low TTL so fakes expire before reaching the server
udp.strategyChecksumDesc: Invalid UDP checksum so the server drops fakes
udp.fakeCountHelper: Number of fake packets sent before real packet
udp.fakeSizeHelper: Size of each fake UDP packet payload
udp.fakePayloadFileHelper: Pick a captured payload to use as the fake UDP packet body. Truncated or zero-padded to the size above. Default = zero fill.
udp.fakePayloadFileEmpty: No captures uploaded yet. Default = zero fill.
udp.fakePayloadFileAutoQuic: b4 generates a fresh randomized QUIC Initial for each fake packet, with random connection IDs. Recommended size: 1200 bytes.
udp.fakePayloadManage: Upload or manage payloads in Settings → Payloads
udp.seg2delayHelper: Delay between segments. Use a range for random delay per packet.

dns.sectionDescription: Redirect DNS queries to bypass ISP DNS poisoning
dns.alert: Some ISPs intercept DNS queries (especially to 8.8.8.8) and return fake IPs for blocked domains. DNS redirect transparently rewrites your DNS queries to use an unpoisoned resolver.
dns.enableDesc: Redirect DNS queries for domains in this set to specified DNS server
dns.pinsNotTargeted: This set does not match {{domains}}, so the pin will never be used. A pin only applies to names the set already targets.
dns.pinsHelper: Hosts file order, one line per address: the address first, then the names it should answer for. Covers each name and its subdomains, and wins over the resolver below.
dns.pinsAlert: When a CDN keeps answering with an address the firewall drops, no bypass strategy reaches the server, because nothing gets there at all. Pinning an address that does answer replaces what DNS hands out for that name, with no hosts file to edit on every device.
dns.noDohWarning: Select or enter a DoH URL to enable redirect.
dns.fragmentQueryDesc: Split DNS packets using IP fragmentation to bypass DPI that pattern-matches domain names in queries
dns.strict: Fail closed when the resolver is unreachable
dns.strictDesc: Leave this off and b4 answers from the last good reply, or from the resolver the client was already using, whenever the redirect target cannot be reached. Turn it on and the query returns SERVFAIL instead, so nothing in this set resolves while the redirect target is down.
dns.serverIpHelper: Select below or enter custom IP
dns.dohUrlHelper: Resolve matched domains over encrypted DoH. Takes precedence over the DNS server IP above. Useful for resolvers that only serve DoH or whose plain DNS is spoofed by your ISP.
dns.noServerWarning: Select or enter a DNS server IP to enable redirect.
dns.googleWarning: Google DNS (8.8.8.8) is commonly poisoned by Russian ISPs. Consider Quad9 (9.9.9.9) or Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) instead.

routing.sectionDescription: DNS redirect and traffic routing for matched domains
routing.enableDesc: Resolve matched domains and route destination IPs via selected output interface or upstream proxy
routing.modeHelper: Send matched traffic out a network interface, or hand it off to an upstream SOCKS5 proxy (e.g. local Xray/sing-box)
routing.flowMTProtoWSCaption: Matched Telegram traffic is bridged over Telegram's WebSocket edge by B4 - no in-app proxy and no VPS needed.
routing.howItWorksMTProtoWS: When a device connects to a Telegram datacenter, B4 transparently intercepts it and relays the session over Telegram's WebSocket edge (with Cloudflare fallback), so Telegram works without configuring a proxy inside the app. Pair this with the 'telegram' geoip target. Uses the shared 'Telegram upstream' settings (Settings -> MTProto), which apply even when the proxy server is off. Best-effort: only TCP MTProto is bridged (voice calls and unknown transports fall through directly).
routing.infoMTProtoWS: Routing intercepts matched Telegram traffic from the source interfaces above and bridges it over the WebSocket edge. Connections B4 cannot map to a datacenter fall open to a direct connection.
routing.mtprotoWsNote: This mode runs on its own - the MTProto proxy under Settings -> MTProto does not need to be enabled. Matched Telegram traffic is relayed over B4's built-in WebSocket endpoint, with a Cloudflare fallback.
routing.blockActionHelper: How matched traffic is blocked. Reject fails the connection immediately (TCP reset, or ICMP unreachable for UDP/QUIC); Drop is silent.
routing.flowBlockCaption: Matched destinations are dropped or rejected by B4 - traffic never leaves the router.
routing.howItWorksBlock: When a device on your network connects to a matched domain or IP, B4 blocks it outright instead of routing it anywhere. Add ad/tracker domains, IPs, or geo categories to this set's targets. 'Reject' (the default) fails the connection instantly (TCP reset, or ICMP unreachable for UDP/QUIC); 'Drop' silently blackholes it so the connection just times out. Works for both LAN devices (forward) and the router itself (output).
routing.infoBlock: Routing blocks this set's matched domains and IPs. No output interface or upstream is needed.
routing.outputInterfaceHelper: Select egress interface for this set
routing.egressIpHelper: Rewrite the source address of this set's traffic. Leave empty to keep the interface's own address.
routing.egressIpNote: This set leaves through {{iface}} with source {{ip}}. B4 puts that address on {{iface}} for you and takes it back afterwards. The device upstream still has to route that source into the path you want - B4 only stamps it.
routing.upstreamHostHelper: Hostname or IP of the SOCKS5 proxy. Use 127.0.0.1 if Xray/sing-box runs on the same router.
routing.upstreamAuthHelper: Leave empty if the upstream proxy does not require authentication
routing.useDomainDesc: When B4 already knows the domain for the destination IP (from prior DNS), pass the domain to the upstream so it can resolve and pick a geo-correct IP. Recommended.
routing.failOpen: Fall back to direct on upstream failure
routing.failOpenDesc: If the upstream proxy is unreachable, open a plain direct connection to the original destination instead of failing.
routing.failOpenWarning: Fail-open exposes the destination to your ISP if the upstream goes down. Disable for whitelist-mode regions where direct connections do not work and you want failures to be visible.
routing.udpDesc: Also tunnel matched UDP traffic through the upstream SOCKS5 proxy (via UDP ASSOCIATE), not just TCP. Applies to forwarded traffic from LAN clients. Most SOCKS5 proxies are TCP-only, and Xray/sing-box need UDP enabled on the inbound. Leave off for TCP-only routing: B4 then refuses QUIC (UDP/443) to matched addresses so clients fall back to TCP and stay on the proxy.
routing.proxyManipulationNote: In proxy mode B4 leaves the packets of matched traffic alone: no faking, fragmentation or desync, and no SYN health check, dead-IP escalation, IP block detection or TCP duplication. The upstream proxy handles obfuscation.
routing.flowProxyCaption: Matched traffic is handed off to the upstream SOCKS5 proxy. The proxy is responsible for reaching the destination.
routing.howItWorksProxy: When a device on your network visits a matched domain, B4 intercepts the connection and forwards it through the upstream SOCKS5 proxy you configure. Use this to chain B4 into Xray/sing-box running locally on the router or on another host. Useful in regions with whitelist-based blocking where direct connections to non-whitelisted IPs are dropped.
routing.ipTtlHelper: How long resolved A/AAAA addresses stay in routing set
routing.sourceInterfacesHint: Limit marking to ingress interfaces (empty = any interface)
routing.unavailableWarning: Output interface "{{iface}}" is down or missing. Routing for this set will not work until it is available again or you select another interface.
routing.info: Routing uses DNS answers for this set domains. Route marks and table IDs are assigned automatically per output interface.
routing.infoProxy: Routing uses DNS answers for this set domains. Matched traffic is hijacked from the source interfaces above and forwarded to the upstream proxy.
routing.flowCaption: DNS queries for this set's domains are intercepted. Resolved IPs are routed through the selected output interface.
routing.howItWorks: When a device on your network visits a matched domain, B4 intercepts the DNS response, learns the destination IP, and adds a routing rule so that traffic to that IP goes through the output interface you choose - for example, a VPN or a different WAN link.
routing.sourceInterfacesDesc: Choose which network interfaces B4 should watch for traffic. For example, select your LAN or Wi-Fi bridge to only route traffic from devices on that network. Leave empty to route traffic from all interfaces.
routing.ipTtlDesc: After B4 learns an IP address from a DNS response, it keeps the routing rule for this many seconds. If the domain's IP changes (e.g. CDN rotation), the old rule expires and B4 picks up the new IP on the next DNS query.
routing.domainOnlyConflict: Domain-only matching is on, so this set routes only the IP addresses you list explicitly. Routing picks traffic by destination address, before the domain name is visible, so a set that learns no addresses routes nothing. Turning it off routes these domains, and with them every other domain that shares the same CDN address.
routing.noDestination: This set has no domain or IP target, so there is nothing for the firewall to steer and no rule is installed. Routing rules always match a destination address.
routing.noDestinationWithDevices: This set selects source devices but has no domain or IP target. Source devices decide whose traffic is offered to the routing rule, not which traffic is steered, so nothing is routed and no rule is installed. To send everything from those devices, turn on "Match any IP address" under Targets, IP addresses.
routing.routerTrafficHelper: Whether connections the router itself opens to this set's destinations also go out the output interface.
routing.routerTrafficScoped: This set is already limited to a source interface or device, and the router's own traffic comes from neither, so it always stays on the normal route.
routing.routerTrafficLoopWarning: {{iface}} is a tunnel a program on this router reads. If that program answers a routed connection by opening its own to the same address, B4 sends it straight back into {{iface}} and the loop will eat all the memory on the device. Switch back to Automatic, or pick a source interface or device for this set.
routing.routerTrafficHeldBack: {{iface}} is a tunnel a program on this router reads, so B4 leaves the router's own traffic on the normal route. Routing it into {{iface}} would come back out as a new connection to the same address and loop.
routing.killSwitchDesc: If the output interface goes away, drop this set's traffic instead of letting it fall back to the normal uplink.
routing.tunnelManipulationNote: {{iface}} wraps the packet before anything on the network sees it, so B4 leaves this set's packets alone: no faking, fragmentation or desync, and no SYN health check, dead-IP escalation, IP block detection or TCP duplication. The settings on the Strategy tabs have no effect while the set routes there. Such connections are tagged routed->{{iface}} in the connection log.

importExport.importSuccess: Configuration imported successfully! Review your changes in the other tabs, then click Save to apply.
importExport.infoAlert: Copy JSON to share this set, or paste a configuration to import it.
importExport.jsonHelper: Paste or type a set configuration JSON to import it.
importExport.deviceFilterWarning: This set has source device filters configured. They are excluded from export as they are device-specific.
importExport.invalidFields: Invalid set configuration: missing required fields
importExport.missingPayloads_one: This set points to a payload file that does not exist on this device: {{files}}. Fake packets fall back to a built-in payload, so the set behaves differently than on the machine it was exported from. Ask the author for the .bin file and upload it under the same name.
importExport.missingPayloads_other: This set points to payload files that do not exist on this device: {{files}}. Fake packets fall back to a built-in payload, so the set behaves differently than on the machine it was exported from. Ask the author for the .bin files and upload them under the same names.

editor.escalateNeedsRstProtection: Tip: also enable RST Injection Protection in the TCP tab. It helps keep the current page working while b4 detects the block.

escalation.sectionDescription: If this set keeps failing to reach a website, b4 switches that website to another set. It reacts to a stalled TLS handshake, forged resets, a destination that stops answering, and DNS answers that carry no usable address.
escalation.rstThresholdHelper: How many resets that b4 judges forged, for the same site, before it switches over.
escalation.rstWindowHelper: Resets only count if they happen within this time. Older ones are forgotten.
escalation.ttlHelper: After switching, the site stays on the backup set for this long. Then b4 tries this set again.
escalation.triggersHelper: Each trigger counts on its own. Whichever one reaches its limit first switches the website over.
escalation.stallThresholdHelper: How many times the same connection resends its ClientHello without an answer before b4 switches over.
escalation.stallTimeoutHelper: A resent ClientHello older than this also counts as a stalled handshake.
escalation.dnsThresholdHelper: How many NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL or address-less answers for the same domain before b4 asks the backup set to resolve it.

convert.title: Import from another tool
convert.subtitle: Translate a byedpi or zapret command line into b4 sets
convert.disclaimer: b4 is an independent implementation, not a fork of byedpi or zapret, so this is a best-effort translation rather than an exact copy. Every option is reported below with what it became. Run Discovery afterwards to verify and tune the result.
convert.inputHelper: Paste a command line, a systemd ExecStart= line, or a whole configuration file such as /opt/zapret/config or nfqws.conf.
convert.domainsHelper: Comma separated. They go to the first set that has no host list of its own; give the others their own domains below. A b4 set without targets matches nothing.

warning.ambiguousVersion: The version could not be determined from the options used, and {{flags}} mean different things across byedpi versions. Pick the version explicitly if the result looks wrong.
warning.needsTargets: None of the {{sets}} converted sets has domains or IPs. {{tool}} applies its profiles to everything it sees, while a b4 set only acts on the targets you give it. Add domains on the Targets tab; a set that is reached only through escalation does not need any.
warning.udpDisabledUpstream: UDP was disabled in the source configuration. The UDP settings of the converted sets are left at their defaults.
warning.profilesAsSets: The source configuration has {{count}} profiles. Each one became a separate set, in the same order. Where the source retries a failed connection through the next profile, the sets are linked by escalation and only the first one takes targets.
warning.shadowedSets: {{count}} set(s) claim domains that an earlier set already claims. {{tool}} picks a profile per packet using its port and protocol filters, while b4 picks one set per destination by domain and does not fall through to the next. Profiles that share a host list but differ only by port cannot all apply. The later ones are created disabled - give each the domains it should handle, or delete the ones you do not need.
warning.nothingRecognized: None of the options that actually do the bypass were recognized, so no set would carry a strategy. This looks like a {{tool}} variant with a different option syntax. Send the configuration to the b4 issue tracker so support can be added.
warning.sourceLayout: The text was read as a {{layout}} configuration file. The command line was rebuilt from {{vars}} in the order that launcher uses, so the profiles match what the source tool actually runs.
warning.foreignDaemonVars: {{vars}} configure a different daemon than {{tool}} and were left out of the conversion. Convert them separately if you need them.
warning.alternativeStrategies: The source file has {{count}} commented-out alternative strategies for {{vars}}. They were not converted - uncomment the one you want and analyze again to import it instead.
warning.setsWithoutStrategy: {{count}} set(s) carry no bypass options at all, so they pass traffic through unchanged.
warning.unusedVars: {{vars}} carry options but are not variables {{tool}} reads, so they were left out of the conversion. Rename them or paste their contents on their own if they should be converted.
warning.catchAllProfile: {{count}} profile(s) have no host list of their own. In {{tool}} such a profile handles everything the others did not match; a b4 set with no targets matches nothing instead, so it is created disabled.

reason.proxyRuntime: Configures the byedpi proxy process itself. b4 works on packets in the firewall, so there is nothing to carry over.
reason.resolverBehaviour: Controls how the byedpi proxy handles hostnames in incoming requests. It has no counterpart in b4.
reason.autoRetryTiming: Tunes byedpi's own retry timing. b4 escalation uses its own RST threshold and time window instead.
reason.globalTTL: Sets the TTL of every outgoing connection. b4 only changes the TTL of fake packets.
reason.processControl: Process management for the source daemon.
reason.noEquivalent: b4 has no equivalent for this option.
reason.profileCopy: Replays another profile's options. Expand it in the source command line and convert again.
reason.unmappedTarget: Recognized, but the converter has no rule for it yet.
reason.unknownOption: Not a known option for this tool and version.
reason.ambiguousOption: Abbreviated option name matches more than one option.
reason.missingValue: The option needs a value but none was given.
reason.badValue: The value could not be parsed: {{detail}}
reason.noIPv6Mapped: IPv6 is excluded, so the set is limited to IPv4.
reason.noUDPUpstream: UDP forwarding was disabled in the source. b4 handles UDP per set instead.
reason.delayMapped: Became the inter-packet delay between fragments.
reason.fakeSNIMapped: b4 generates a ClientHello for this hostname and uses it as the fake packet.
reason.fakeSNINormalised: "{{from}}" is not a hostname. Read as {{to}}, which is what b4 generates the fake ClientHello for.
reason.fakeSNINotAHost: This value is not a hostname, so no fake payload could be generated from it.
reason.hostsMapped: {{count}} domain(s) became the targets of this set.
reason.hostsFileUnresolved: Reads the host list from {{path}}, which is not available here. Add the domains on the Targets tab.
reason.ipsMapped: The addresses became the IP targets of this set.
reason.ipsetFileUnresolved: Reads the address list from {{path}}, which is not available here. Add the addresses on the Targets tab.
reason.portFilterMapped: Became the destination port filter of the set.
reason.protoAsPorts: b4 selects traffic by port rather than by protocol, so the protocol filter became a port filter.
reason.protoUDPOnly: This profile is UDP only, so the set carries UDP handling and no TCP strategy.
reason.udpFakeCount: Became the number of fake UDP packets b4 sends.
reason.tlsRecMapped: Became TLS record splitting at this position.
reason.disoobNoOOB: Disorder with an out-of-band byte is not available in b4. The disorder part is kept, the OOB byte is dropped.
reason.oobMapped: Became out-of-band splitting at this position, using byedpi's default OOB byte.
reason.oobDroppedForCombo: A set uses one splitting method at a time, and another one was selected for this profile. The OOB split is dropped.
reason.singleStrategyOnly: A set uses one splitting method at a time, and another one was selected for this profile.
reason.repeatsWithoutSkip: The repeat count has no step, so every repetition lands on the same offset. This does nothing in byedpi either, and nothing was carried over.
reason.repeatsUnsupported: Repeats the split {{repeats}} times with a step of {{skip}} bytes. b4 splits at fixed points instead, so only the first position was kept.
reason.sniMiddleMapped: Splits in the middle of the hostname.
reason.sniAnchorApproximated: Anchored at {{position}}. b4 splits in the middle of the hostname, which is the closest equivalent.
reason.httpHostAnchor: Anchored on the HTTP Host header. b4 splits on the TLS hostname instead.
reason.packetAnchorApproximated: Anchored at {{position}} inside the packet. b4 splits relative to the hostname instead.
reason.negativeOffset: Counts backwards from the end of the packet. b4 counts from the start of the TLS payload, so hostname splitting was used instead.
reason.zeroOffset: An offset of 0 means no split.
reason.fixedPositionIgnored: This splitting method uses hostname-relative split points in b4, so the fixed offset was dropped.
reason.positionClamped: The offset is beyond the range b4 accepts and was clamped.
reason.requiresFake: Only affects fake packets, and this profile sends none.
reason.fakeMapped: Enables fake packets before the real ClientHello. byedpi places the fake at {{position}}; b4 sends it as a separate packet with a low TTL.
reason.fakeTTLMapped: Became the TTL of the fake packets.
reason.md5sigMapped: Adds a TCP MD5 option to the fake packet.
reason.fakeDataFileUnresolved: Reads the fake payload from {{path}}, which is not available here. A built-in payload is used instead.
reason.fakeTLSModUnsupported: This fake ClientHello modification has no counterpart in b4.
reason.fakeOffsetUnsupported: Shifts where the fake data starts. b4 sends the fake as a whole packet, so there is no offset to set.
reason.ipOptUnsupported: Adds IP options to the fake packet. b4 has no equivalent.
reason.dropSackMapped: Removes the SACK option from TCP packets.
reason.httpTamper: Rewrites HTTP request headers. b4 does not modify plaintext HTTP.
reason.roundUnsupported: Selects which request in a connection to act on. b4 uses a packet limit per connection instead.
reason.escalateMapped: Starts a new profile that runs when the previous one fails. Became an escalation link between the two sets.
reason.escalateTriggersPartial: Became an escalation link between the two sets. b4 escalates on repeated RSTs; the HTTP redirect and TLS error triggers have no counterpart.
reason.autoNoneAsSeparateSet: Starts a profile that runs when the previous one does not match. It became a separate set rather than an escalation step.
reason.firstByteMapped: Became a split after the first byte.
reason.splitPointsCollapsed: The source configuration splits at {{count}} positions here. A b4 set has a fixed set of split points and cannot reproduce an arbitrary ladder, so the closest available ones were selected.
reason.profileWithoutDesync: This profile carries no bypass options, so it passes traffic through unchanged - the same thing the source tool does when it falls back to this group.
reason.unaccountedOption: Recognized, but nothing in the converted set came out of it. Report the command line so a rule can be added.
reason.udpFoldedIntoSet: The UDP-only profile carries no targets of its own, so its UDP handling was folded into this set. Kept as a separate set it would have matched the same TCP traffic first and passed it through untouched.
reason.autoNoneEntrySet: Starts the profile that handles everything the previous one did not. It is the entry set here.
reason.desyncModesMapped: The desync modes became the strategy of this set.
reason.desyncModesDropped: b4 has no equivalent for {{dropped}}, so that part of the mode list was dropped.
reason.desyncModesEmpty: None of these modes produced anything b4 can apply.
reason.foolingMapped: The fooling method became the way b4 makes the fake packet unusable to the server.
reason.foolingPartial: A set has one faking strategy. {{kept}} was kept, {{dropped}} dropped.
reason.fakeRepeatsMapped: Became the number of fake packets sent before the real one.
reason.udpFakeRepeatsMapped: Became the number of fake UDP packets.
reason.seqOvlPatternMapped: The overlap pattern was read as raw bytes; a TLS 1.2 header is used when it cannot be parsed.
reason.wsSizeApproximated: Shrinks the window b4 advertises to the server so it sends smaller segments. b4 has no equivalent, so the closest thing was used: fake ACK packets with a zero window.
reason.skipMapped: The profile is marked skipped, so the set is created disabled.
reason.newProfileAsSet: Starts a new profile. Each one became a separate set, in the same order.
reason.sniExtMapped: Splits right before the SNI extension.
reason.sniExtApproximated: Anchored on the SNI extension with an offset. b4 splits exactly at the extension or in the middle of the hostname, so the offset was dropped.
reason.ipVersionMapped: Limits the set to one IP version.
reason.l7QUICMapped: b4 selects UDP traffic by QUIC parsing rather than by an L7 filter.
reason.l7FilterApproximated: b4 selects traffic by port and by domain rather than by an L7 protocol filter.
reason.fakeQUICApproximated: b4 generates a fresh QUIC Initial per packet instead of replaying a captured one. Upload the file under Settings, Payloads to use the original.
reason.fakeHexPayload: The fake payload is a raw hex pattern. b4 carries a generated ClientHello, a preset, an all-zero payload or an uploaded capture, so an arbitrary pattern has no counterpart. Upload it under Settings, Payloads to use it.
reason.tcpOnlyFakeOption: Only affects TCP fakes, and this profile handles UDP.
reason.negatedPortFilter: b4 port filters list the ports to act on and cannot express a negation.
reason.excludeListUnsupported: b4 has no exclusion list. Remove the entries from the set targets instead.
reason.autoTTLUnsupported: Picks the fake TTL from the measured hop count. b4 uses a fixed TTL, so set it by hand or let Discovery find it.
reason.origPacketTTL: Changes the TTL of the real packets. b4 only changes the TTL of fake ones.
reason.packetWindowUnsupported: Limits the desync to a range of packets in the connection. b4 uses a per-connection packet limit instead.
reason.ipFragPosition: Sets the IP fragmentation offset. b4 chooses it itself.
reason.dupKnobUnsupported: b4 duplication sends plain copies and has no separate TTL, fooling or window of its own.
reason.hostlistAuto: zapret builds this host list itself by watching for blocks. b4 has Watchdog and Discovery for that.
reason.httpFakePayload: A fake payload for plaintext HTTP. b4 fakes TLS and QUIC only.
reason.engineDetail: Configures how nfqws attaches to the firewall. b4 manages that itself.
reason.anyProtocol: Acts on any data packet rather than only HTTP and TLS. b4 works from the TLS ClientHello and the QUIC Initial.
reason.ssidFilter: Applies the profile only on certain Wi-Fi networks. b4 has no equivalent.
reason.windowsOnly: Only applies to the Windows build of zapret.
reason.shadowedByEarlierSet: {{other}} already claims {{domain}}. b4 picks one set per destination and does not fall back to the next, so this set would never run. It is created disabled - give it its own domains to use it.
reason.ipv6OnlyKnob: Sets the hop limit for IPv6 desync packets separately. b4 uses one TTL for both address families.
reason.fakeTLSModPartial: Kept what b4 has an equivalent for. Dropped: {{dropped}}.
reason.templatePlaceholder: A placeholder from the configuration template. It is substituted before the daemon runs, so there is nothing to convert.
reason.udpOnlySetNotProtocolScoped: This profile only filters UDP, but a b4 set is not limited to one protocol. If you give it domains it will also claim them for TCP, taking them away from the TCP sets. Leave it without targets unless it is the only set for those domains.
reason.profileNotUnderstood: {{count}} option(s) in this profile were not recognized, and nothing else in it produced a strategy. The set is created disabled so it cannot claim domains while doing nothing.
reason.fakeTTLOriginal: A TTL of 0 means the fake keeps the TTL of the real packet, so b4 leaves it alone too.
reason.repeatedOptionCombined: The option appears {{count}} times in this profile and every value applies; they were combined into one setting.
reason.supersededByLater: Given again later as {{winner}}, and that is the value that applies. This one has no effect.
reason.extraSplitPositionDropped: A set splits at one point for the strategy it uses, and another option already supplied it. This position was dropped.
reason.everyPortMatched: Acts on every port, which is what a b4 set does when its port filter is empty.
reason.seqOvlLengthUnsupported: b4 overlaps a fixed number of bytes counted from the start of the payload, so a relative or non-positive length has no counterpart.
reason.fakeZeroPayloadOverridden: b4 has an all-zero fake payload, but another option in this profile supplies the payload instead, so that one was used.
reason.fakeUnknownUDPApproximated: Became the UDP fake payload. b4 carries one payload per set and generates a fresh QUIC Initial per packet instead of replaying a captured one.
reason.anyProtocolUDP: Became UDP faking for every protocol rather than QUIC alone. b4 has no counterpart on the TCP side, where it acts on TLS.
reason.detachedOptionValue: {{option}} takes its value written with =, so this word is not read as its value. nfqws ignores it in the same way.
reason.zapret2Lua: zapret2 keeps its bypass strategies in Lua scripts rather than in options, and b4 cannot read them.
reason.tlsRecAnchorApproximated: Splits the TLS record at an offset from the hostname. b4 splits its TLS record around the hostname itself, so the offset was dropped.
reason.oobAnchorApproximated: Sends the out-of-band byte at an offset from the hostname. b4 sends it in the middle of the hostname, so the offset was dropped.
reason.requiresOOB: Only affects out-of-band splitting, and this set uses another splitting method.
reason.fakeSplitBoundaryLost: The fake position also splits the request upstream. This set sends fake packets but passes the real request whole, since no other option asked for a split.
reason.escalationTargetIdentical: This set ends up identical to {{other}}, so escalating from it would change nothing. The escalation link was removed.
reason.portFilterDroppedOnFallback: A set reached only through escalation carries no port filter of its own, so the ports from this profile were dropped.
reason.positionInRange: Falls inside the range of offsets the set splits at. b4 picks one offset from that range per packet rather than splitting at all of them.

descriptions.sni: Finds bypass SNI values for blocked ASNs by brute-forcing whitelist domains

descriptions.telegram: Measures Telegram download/upload throughput and datacenter reachability

meanings.DNS_SPOOFING: UDP DNS returns a different IP than DoH (spoofing)
meanings.DNS_INTERCEPTION: UDP DNS is intercepted or times out while DoH works
meanings.FAKE_NXDOMAIN: UDP returns NXDOMAIN while DoH resolves the domain
meanings.FAKE_EMPTY: UDP returns an empty answer while DoH resolves the domain
meanings.BOTH_UNAVAILABLE: Neither UDP nor DoH resolution is available
meanings.TLS_SPOOF: Non-TLS or garbage response injected in place of TLS
meanings.TLS_ALERT: Forged TLS alert (e.g. unrecognized name / handshake failure)
meanings.TLS_RST: Connection reset during or after the TLS handshake
meanings.SYN_DROP: TCP SYN dropped, connection never established
meanings.TCP16: Connection dropped within the 12-69KB TSPU fat-flow window
meanings.ISP_PAGE: Redirected to an ISP block page
meanings.FOUND: A working bypass SNI was found
meanings.NOT_BLOCKED: ASN was not blocked, no brute-force needed
